$schema-note: One theme preset (design brief 2026-08-27, §4.2). A preset is a complete designed look: two authored palettes, a type map for all four roles, shape and texture and density, a motif default, and the curated option sets from the visual story.
$palette-note: Channels are [r, g, b] numbers, never hex strings — the generator writes the RGB triples (brief §3.6). The dark palette is authored value by value; no dark value is derived from its light twin.
$first-class-note: See design/tokens/presets/civic.json: all six styles are first-class, each with one recommended configuration.
label: Newsroom
summary: A well-made news site on a good day. Named sections, one strong rule each, numbers that never borrow the headline face.
bestFor: Publications, media summits, and newsrooms that put something out every day.
$palette-words-light: cool newsprint white, desk black, one saturated editorial accent, muted data slate, hairline silver, section-rule graphite, caption grey, archive fog
$palette-words-dark: charcoal desk, screen-lit soft white, night-retuned editorial accent, dimmed data slate, graphite rule, ash grey, low-lamp caption grey, archive slate
$font-note: Brief §4.2. Plex Sans handles captions and data so numbers never borrow the headline face; Plex Mono carries the figure column.
$tokens-note: Preset-level remaps of existing tier 2 and tier 3 tokens. No new property name (brief §3.4).

choices.label: Fraunces
choices.why: The designed headline. Its soft-serif wonk is what makes the site read as edited rather than generated.

choices.label: Newsreader at display weights
choices.why: The wire-service desk. Running the body face up to headline size gives a quieter, more traditional publication that still belongs to the same newsroom.

choices.label: Archivo bold condensed
choices.why: Grotesque headlines are a real newsroom tradition, and they keep the story while letting a client trade warmth for punch.

choices.label: Rule-bounded bar
choices.why: Name left, dates right, the strong rule under the whole bar. The standing masthead of a site that publishes every day.

choices.label: Stacked with a deck
choices.why: The deck is a newsroom device, not marketing copy, so it must state a fact about the event.

choices.label: Section-aware bar
choices.why: The running head of a news site; it reinforces the table-of-contents idea the section rules set up.

component.label: Schedule style
component.prompt: How a session listing is set.

choices.label: Hairline row
choices.why: A hairline-separated row with title, time, track, speaker. The listing of a publication.

choices.label: Lead and rest
choices.why: The lead story and the digest under it, which is how a news page ranks things without cards, shadows, or colored edges.
